intro: Two extensions of the relative clause. First, possession: dessen (after a masculine or neuter noun) and deren (after a feminine or plural noun) mean "whose" — der Kollege, dessen Frau …; die Nachbarin, deren Hund …; die Familien, deren Häuser … . They never change for case, and the noun that follows takes its ending as if no article were there: dessen neuer Roman, deren alte Wohnung. Second, relative clauses with a preposition: the preposition comes first, then the relative pronoun in the case the preposition demands — die Firma, bei der …; der Freund, mit dem …; das Thema, über das …; die Kolleginnen, von denen … . The relative pronoun takes its gender and number from the noun it refers to, but its case from its job inside the relative clause. When the reference is not a noun but alles, etwas, nichts or a whole clause, the preposition fuses with wo(r)-: etwas, worüber …; alles, wofür … . English often hides the preposition at the end ("the town I grew up in"); German always puts it at the front of the clause.
tips[0].title: dessen / deren = whose
tips[0].text: Masculine or neuter noun → dessen; feminine or plural noun → deren. The form looks at the owner (the noun before the comma), not at the thing owned: der Mann, dessen Tochter …; die Frau, deren Sohn …; die Kinder, deren Eltern … .
tips[0].trap: "whose" does not agree with the thing owned. die Nachbarin, deren Hund — not dessen Hund, even though Hund is masculine.
tips[0].check.why: The owner, die Ärztin, is feminine, so 'whose' is deren, whatever the gender of Praxis.
tips[1].title: Preposition + relative pronoun: gender from the noun, case from the preposition
tips[1].text: die Firma (f), bei (Dat) → bei der · der Freund (m), mit (Dat) → mit dem · das Thema (n), über (Akk) → über das · die Kolleginnen (Pl), von (Dat) → von denen · der Termin (m), auf (Akk) → auf den. The preposition always stands at the start of the relative clause.
tips[1].check.why: The preposition goes first; Kollege is masculine and auf here takes the accusative: auf den. wo(r)- is not used for people.
tips[1].visual.rows[0].b: die Leute, mit denen ich arbeite
tips[1].visual.rows[1].b: das Thema, über das wir gesprochen haben
tips[2].title: Dative plural: denen; possession after a preposition: mit dessen …
tips[2].text: The relative pronoun has two long forms: denen (dative plural) and dessen / deren (genitive). With a preposition before dessen / deren, the following noun takes the case of that preposition: mit dessen Roman, in deren Wohnung.
tips[2].check.why: mit takes the dative, and the dative plural relative pronoun is denen.
tips[3].title: Turn the English round
tips[3].text: "the woman I gave the key to" → the preposition or case goes to the front: die Frau, der ich den Schlüssel gegeben habe. "something you will be pleased about" → etwas, worüber du dich freust.
tips[3].check.why: The English 'to' becomes the dative at the front of the clause: jemandem etwas leihen → dem.

remember[0]: dessen after der/das-nouns, deren after die-nouns and plurals — the owner decides.
remember[1]: Preposition first; gender from the noun, case from the preposition; dative plural denen.
mistakes[0].why: The owner (die Nachbarin) is feminine → deren.
mistakes[1].why: The preposition goes to the front, followed by the relative pronoun.
mistakes[2].why: The dative plural relative pronoun is denen.
hook: Say 'whose' and 'the people I work with' in German: dessen, deren, and the preposition right at the front.
recall.today: dessen and deren after a preposition: mit dessen Hilfe, in deren Haus.
